summary: Veridis Defense, a California LLC in Beverly Hills, is designing a swarm of 5 to 15 autonomous firefighting multirotors run by one operator through a console called AD.OS. Its news posts say it ran as AdAstra Defense until September 2026. Its site says the fleet is in prototyping and the software is simulation-verified.
thesis: An autonomy and drone company aimed at early wildfire and structure fire response for fire agencies. No funding was found, so this would be a first-cheque decision on a two-founder team with no published flight evidence.
stage: Formation stage, no funding found. The Energy Tech Summit write-up of an April 2026 pitch in Bilbao says the company, then AdAstra Defense, had no outside funding and was raising $3 million pre-seed on a safe note. The AdAstra site, live on 2 October 2026, says "Raising $3M Seed". EDGAR searches on 2 October 2026 returned no match for either name. No source opened names an investor.

team.name: Gabriel Klein
team.background: Co-founder and CEO per the Veridis site, which describes his role as company vision and government partnerships. No source opened gives prior work history.

team.name: Patrick Krzysztofik
team.background: Co-founder and CTO per the Veridis site, which says he designs every product and builds the aircraft prototypes and software stack solo.

team.name: Douglas Loewe
team.background: Advisor per the Veridis site, which describes him as former CEO of KAO Data with 20+ years as a global executive.

team.name: Hubert Krzysztofik
team.background: Listed as co-founder and CTO on the earlier AdAstra Defense site, which is still live. He does not appear on the Veridis site, which names two founders.

questions: The AdAstra site lists four co-founders and three advisers, the Veridis site two founders and one adviser. What changed, who left, and who holds the equity and IP?
What has flown? Which of Ember, Cinder and Vulcan exist as hardware today, and are flight logs or raw video available before the demo film?
Is the $3 million pre-seed raise still open, on what terms, and is any committed? Is Veridis Defense LLC the same legal entity as the earlier AdAstra company?
Which fire agencies have you spoken to, and is there a signed pilot or letter of intent? Under which FAA authority would a first pilot fly?
risks: No flight evidence is published. The home page labels its headline metrics as target, simulated or design. No customer, pilot or investor is named in any source opened.
The earlier site credited DARPA swarm experience to a CTO and two advisers not on the Veridis site, which says one founder builds the hardware and software stack solo.
Regulatory approvals are not held. The compliance page marks Part 137 certification for suppressant dispensing as scoped but not yet held and Part 107 operations as a pathway.
unverified: The company's news posts describe a rename, but no filing read confirms that Veridis Defense LLC is the renamed Adastra Defense LLC rather than a new entity.
The AdAstra site gives Hubert Krzysztofik's background as co-founding Infinite Reality, a "$10.1B exit" and the DARPA OFFSET program. No primary page confirming it was opened.
The AdAstra site says the team designed, built and field-tested multiple heat-resistant prototype systems and built the full software stack. No independent evidence was found.
